clue.text: Hit an alien, given new order to destroy

indicators.note: letters given a new order are rearranged into a different sequence

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to strike an alien and wipe it out, like a science-fiction battle command.
explanation.definitionFit: To annihilate is to wipe out completely, a direct synonym for destroying something.

clue.text: Assistant's brainwave, moving article from bottom to top

indicators.text: moving article from bottom to top
indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so the final article is shifted round to the front

parts.note: a brainwave is a sudden idea

explanation.surface: Someone's helper has had a brilliant idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is A, the last letter of the brainwave word, which rises to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, typically to an official.

clue.text: Kind of family crazy uncle and aunt rule, primarily

indicators.note: crazy suggests something wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters are used

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A family in which a mad uncle and an aunt hold sway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear family is one made of parents and children only, so nuclear names a kind of family.

clue.text: Animal, one of particular colour, seen in tree

parts.note: a chestnut is a horse of a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A brown animal spotted up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is a horse described by its coat colour, so the clue really says horse twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a large tree that produces conkers.

clue.text: Creates boundary — in length, it's under one mile

indicators.note: in a down entry under means placed below, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A rule saying a boundary must be under a mile long.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to set a boundary on it, so limits means sets a boundary.

clue.text: Produce some spin, perhaps, for aggressive business deal

parts.note: a take is a yield or catch, what is produced
in cricket an over is a set of six balls, which a spin bowler may deliver

explanation.surface: A company spinning its story to justify a hostile bid.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin is cricket here: an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler, and a spinner bowls spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile takeover is when one company buys control of another against its management's wishes.

clue.text: They measure resistance from government department, initially

definitions.meaning: first meaning: units of electrical resistance
second meaning: the initials of On Her Majesty's Service, printed on official British government mail

explanation.surface: Someone noting that a government department's meters gauge resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: OHMS was stamped on letters sent from British government departments, standing for On Her Majesty's Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohms are the units in which electrical resistance is measured; the same letters abbreviate the official postal marking.

clue.text: Male left in pit in lowest level for shift, for instance

definitions.text: lowest level for shift, for instance

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside another word, which wraps around it

explanation.surface: A miner left at the bottom of the pit for his working shift.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is a simple dress here, not a work period, so its lowest level is its hem.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline is the bottom edge of a skirt or dress, such as a shift.

clue.text: Bound issue turned up in early part of year

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A publication's edition appearing at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Springtime is the spring season, falling in the early months of the year.

clue.text: Behaviour that's becoming odd — almost lure into trap at first

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
at first says this part comes at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to decoy is to lure into a trap
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A warning that odd behaviour might nearly lure someone into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' belongs to the definition, in its sense of fitting or seemly. Rum is an old British word for peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly conduct, which is exactly behaviour that is becoming or suitable.

clue.text: Arm Sikh that's agitated in region of India

indicators.note: something agitated is stirred up and shaken about, so its letters move

explanation.surface: A call to arm an agitated Sikh in some part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a disputed northern territory, part of which is administered by India.

clue.text: Person consulted expressing no interest, as some might say

indicators.note: says the words should be judged by how they are spoken out loud

explanation.surface: An adviser who is approached but shows no interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding board is someone whose reactions you test ideas on, a person you consult.

clue.text: Shocking process as court badly interrupts political event

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other
something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: an election is a political event

explanation.surface: A scandal: a court case badly disrupts an election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like a judgement on the scandal, but it means delivering electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrocution is killing or injuring by electric shock, a process that is literally shocking.

clue.text: The speaker's standing on section of facade or barrier

indicators.note: in a down entry standing on means sitting on top, so this piece comes first

parts.note: I'm, the speaker is, without the apostrophe
a pediment is the triangular gable on a classical facade

explanation.surface: Someone standing on a building's front, which acts as a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or hindrance, something that blocks progress like a barrier.

clue.text: King Edward, for example, as source of pessimistic law

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slang word for a potato, of which King Edward is a British variety
second meaning: the name behind the law that whatever can go wrong will

explanation.surface: A king named as the origin of a gloomy legal principle.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is not a monarch here but a popular British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy is informal slang for a potato, and Murphy's Law states that anything that can go wrong will.

clue.text: Exhausted layabout

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as two words, utterly worn out
second meaning: an idle, feckless person

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it is the adjective for tired out; as one word it is a noun for an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead beat means completely tired, while a deadbeat is a lazy, unreliable person who avoids work.

clue.text: Blue during fall, after last of deciduous leaves

indicators.note: after places the remaining piece behind the first one

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so that letter is removed
last of means only the final letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Blue skies during autumn, after the last of the deciduous leaves have fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb: the letter departs. Blue means risqué here.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is smutty or risqué, which is indecent material.

clue.text: Passing within three laps, in general

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A general observation about something going by in the space of three laps.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapsing is time passing by, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: You finally invested in case it has lots to offer

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a legal case is an action

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: An investment pitch promising a case with plenty to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' are the numbered items put up for sale, not plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a sale where goods are offered in numbered lots to bidders.

clue.text: Do some singing, playing well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sing is slang for telling tales to the police
second meaning: as two words, a sports phrase for being in good condition

explanation.surface: A performer singing and playing well.
explanation.walkthrough: Singing here is criminal slang for informing, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone is to sing, in underworld slang; a player in form is performing well.

clue.text: A couple of cricket events go on too long

parts.note: first cricket event: an over, a set of six balls
second cricket event: a run scored

explanation.surface: A complaint that a cricket match keeps dragging on.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple of events are two cricket terms: an over, a bowler's set of six deliveries, and a run scored between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed the allotted time, as a meeting or broadcast might.

clue.text: Like cliché about phosphorus being important element in diet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

explanation.surface: A claim that phosphorus is a key dietary element, made in tired, clichéd terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' teases the chemistry of phosphorus, but the definition means a basic food.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic food forming the main part of a diet, like rice or bread.

clue.text: Beyond doubt, accomplished by popular argument against trial

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is placed next to the others

explanation.surface: A claim proven beyond doubt in a trial, opposing a popular argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the wordplay goes last: 'accomplished by' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incontestable cannot be disputed, so it is beyond doubt.

clue.text: Some swimming energetically in part of pool

indicators.note: some means a portion of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: People swimming hard in one section of a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is the gene pool, a population's stock of genetic material.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is one unit of heredity, a component of a population's gene pool.

clue.text: Communication from John or Paul, say, in English post

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, which surrounds it

parts.note: a pile is a post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A letter from John or Paul sent by English mail, perhaps from the Beatles.
explanation.walkthrough: John and Paul suggest the Beatles or the apostles; they only stand for a saint, ST. 'Post' is a pile, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, a formal written communication, like those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Couple crossing river, that is plain

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, holding it in the middle

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Two travellers fording a river on open flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide expanse of flat grassland, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Bomb in military vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fail badly, as a show or share price does
second meaning: an armoured fighting vehicle

explanation.surface: An explosive device carried inside an army vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bomb' is the verb meaning flop, not an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank is informal for to fail dismally, as to bomb is; a tank is also an armoured combat vehicle.

clue.text: Where countdown begins before social gathering for those present

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the reading order

parts.note: a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A countdown starting just before a party, to check who has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the collective number of people present at an event.
